name: Hong Kong Countryside Conservation Funding Scheme

funder.name: Countryside Conservation Office, Environment and Ecology Bureau (Hong Kong)

summary: Hong Kong government funding for local non-profits to run countryside conservation projects, including management agreements that improve ecological value of privately owned sites. Rounds invite projects for set themes and locations.
reporting: Inception report within one month of start, half-yearly progress reports with statements of account, annual audited accounts, and a completion report with final audited account.

eligibility.rule: Has legal personality and local tax exemption, or is a local registered non-profit company or post-secondary institution
Matches the 2026 round's specified project types, themes, scopes and locations
Has a project site outside Lantau
MA projects have a management agreement with landowners or tenants and work mainly on private land
BH applications include consent from relevant premises owners or government departments
Does not target a graded historical building for conservation or revitalisation
Does not target listed Hong Kong intangible cultural heritage items

documents: Articles of association or equivalent document
List of principal persons-in-charge and their positions
Documentary proof of management agreement with landowners or tenants, for MA projects
Consent from relevant premises owners or government departments, for BH projects
Publicity programme and Public Access Arrangement Plan, for BH applications

status.quote: The cut-off time of application for this round of application is 5 p.m. on 13 August 2026 (Thursday).

deadline.quote: The cut-off time of application for this round of application is 5 p.m. on 13 August 2026 (Thursday).

applicant_types.quote: provide financial support to local non-profit-making organisations (NPOs) and villagers for organising diverse and innovative conservation activities or projects in the countryside (except Lantau Island)

geography.quote: conservation activities or projects in the countryside (except Lantau Island)

access.quote: Local NPOs which want to apply for funding support under the CCFS to implement any of the above types of projects in eligible sites can submit the completed Application Form

window.quote: is inviting a new round of applications for the following types of projects under prescribed themes, locations and scopes specified below

consortium_required.quote: Each application must be submitted by a single organisation as described in Section 2.3.1 above.

reporting.quote: the applicant shall, within one month after the commencement of the project, submit an inception report to the Secretariat.

eligibility.quote: Eligible applicant and co-organising/ supporting organisations must be local tax-exempt charities having legal personality; local registered and non-profit-making companies or local non-profit-making post-secondary education institutions .
Applications outside the specified project types, prescribed themes, scopes and/or locations mentioned above

the MA projects must involve management agreement between applicants and landowners and/or tenants for exchanging the management rights over their land or their cooperation with financial incentives, and the ecological or nature conservation enhancement activities shall be primarily conducted on private land
the applicant organisation should obtain the consent from relevant premises owner(s)/government department(s) and include the consent in the application
the conservation and/or revitalisation of architectural and cultural aspects of graded historical buildings assessed by the Antiquities Advisory Board are not eligible under the CCFS

items listed in Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Hong Kong and the Intangible Cultural Heritage Inventory published by the Intangible Cultural Heritage Office of the Leisure and Cultural Services Department would not be considered under the CCFS

documents.quote: a copy of the organisation's registration document, a copy of the letter issued by the Inland Revenue Department on tax exemption under Section 88 of the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112), a copy of the articles of association or other equivalent document, and a list of the principal persons-in-charge and their positions
could not provide documentary proof on management agreements with landowners or tenants of the target site for MA projects
the applicant organisation should obtain the consent from relevant premises owner(s)/government department(s) and include the consent in the application
The applicant shall submit a publicity programme and Public Access Arrangement Plan

after_award.quote: For every six months of the project period, the applicants of the CCFS have to provide a half-yearly progress report and a statement of account with projected expenditure once every six months to the Secretariat.
For every year of the project period, they have to additionally provide an annual account audited by Certified Public Accountants (CPA) (practising).

effort.quote: Both the original copy (hard copy) and the soft copy of the completed Application Form should reach the Secretariat of the CCFS (Secretariat) before the cut-off time.
The cut-off time of application for this round of application is 5 p.m. on 13 August 2026 (Thursday).

steps: Application form, sent as hard copy and soft copy
